newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Rival Cambodian parties clash in northwest.
newsitem.headline: Rival Cambodian parties clash in northwest.

text.p: Supporters of the two parties in Cambodia's uneasy coalition have clashed outside the country's second largest city, police and officials said on Friday.
Soldiers and security guards of the royalist FUNCINPEC party and the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) fought at Rengsei, 20 km (12 miles) east of Battambang, late on Thursday.
Vorn Chhunly, the most senior FUNCINPEC police official in Battambang, told reporters that CPP soldiers had captured two FUNCINPEC guards and wounded several others.
"Now we have ordered the FUNCINPEC troops...to protect themselves and to do everything to release the two," he said.
"If they can't, we will send troops from Battambang to fight."
The deputy governor of Battambang province, Serei Kosal, is a FUNCINPEC official and rival of Governor Ung Samy, who supports the CCP, the party of war-torn Cambodia's former communist rulers.
Opposition leader Sam Rainsy, guarded by FUNCINPEC police and soldiers, on Friday opened an office of his unrecognised Khmer Nation Party in Battambang.

Serei Kosal, speaking to reporters during a meeting with Sam Rainsy, said he was not prepared to be pushed around by the CPP, which formed the coalition with FUNCINPEC after narrowly losing U.N.-run 1993 elections to the royalists.

"It is not like before and from this time, don't expect me to withdraw my troops. We must protect ourselves," he said, adding that some 20 FUNCINPEC troops faced about 100 CPP fighters in the commune.
CPP officials in Battambang could not immediately be contacted for comment.

Tensions flared in the province in November after clashes between the CPP and FUNCINPEC left several people wounded. The governor and deputy governor were told to cooperate in holding local and general elections due by the end of 1998.
The ill-feeling has been simmering since, reflecting poor relations between the two parties and their leaders, co-premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh (FUNCINPEC) and Hun Sen (CPP).

Analysts have predicted an alliance ahead of the next elections between FUNCINPEC and the KNP. Sam Rainsy was expelled from FUNCINPEC in 1995 for his criticism of the government and his accusations of high-level corruption.
